newsitem.title: JORDAN: Saudi minister says Israel freezes peace.
newsitem.headline: Saudi minister says Israel freezes peace.

text.p: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal blamed Israel on Tuesday for a breakdown in Middle East peace talks and said an Arab-Israeli economic summit could be fruitless unless Israel changed its policies.

"The economic summit, like the multilateral talks, were aimed at supporting the peace process and creating a suitable atmosphere to move the process forward in a positive way," the prince said on arrival in Jordan for talks with King Hussein.

"But the situation has now been frozen by Israel," he told reporters. "Israel has eliminated the grounds for optimism in this context, as it has eliminated the ideas which formed the basis for the multilateral talks."
He said Arab states had done all they could to support peace in the region.
"Until the situation is clear from the Israeli side, the situation is frozen and the Arabs will not bear responsibility for this," Prince Saud said.

His commments echoed remarks by Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam in Cairo on Monday. Syria and some Gulf Arab states favour postponing this year's MENA summit until Middle East peace talks resume.

The 1997 economic conference, the fourth since the landmark 1991 Madrid Middle East peace conference which launched peace negotiations, is being hosted by the Gulf state of Qatar. Israel attended all three previous conferences.

Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah said in an interview with the Egyptian newspaper Al-Ahram on Tuesday that the Qatar summit was a "rare opportunity and the Jordanian government supports its being held on time regardless of the state in negotations with Israel".

Talks between Israel and the Palestinians have been stalled since March when the Jewish state began building a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and a bomber killed himself and three Israeli women in a Tel Aviv cafe.
